QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_18

question.text: Company X: EBITDA INR 30 crore, 8x EV/EBITDA, debt INR 40 crore, cash INR 10 crore. Equity value:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines Enterprise Value as the value of the business regardless of financing, and gives the bridge: EV = Equity Value + Total Debt (net of cash) + Preference Capital. Rearranging: Equity Value = EV - Debt + Cash. With EBITDA of INR 30 crore at an 8x EV/EBITDA multiple, EV = 30 x 8 = INR 240 crore; Equity Value = 240 - 40 + 10 = INR 210 crore. The Trap: INR 240 crore is the Enterprise Value itself, not equity value — a common error is to stop at EV without adjusting for debt and cash. INR 200 crore and INR 280 crore use incorrect signs on the debt/cash adjustment. Note: The previously keyed answer (INR 200 crore) was an answer-key defect. The key has been corrected to INR 210 crore in line with the workbook's EV-to-equity bridge.
